title: Dispatch LTP 7: Tomorrow’s Paper Names the Man Who Will Close It
summary: The advance issue announces an end to the Chronicle under its editor’s signature.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: A bundle dated 21 September arrived this morning with a notice on its front page: “The Alderwick Chronicle will cease publication on 24 September by order of its editor, Julian Ashcombe.” Below the notice is a forecast of smoke pouring from the pressroom and a crowd gathered at the doors. It names no dead or injured people.

Mr. Ashcombe says he has written no such order. He called the notice an attempt to make him obey a page he has not authorized. He has nevertheless stationed Inspector Voss at the pressroom and ordered all paper stock moved away from the old forme.

Dr. Saye found fresh type impressions on the forme’s blank strips. They include the editor’s name, the word “ceases,” and a partial line that might refer to a lamp. Miss Marsh traced a thin silver residue from the iron to the underside of the press. She believes the forme now makes new copies while the regular press stands idle.

The staff has proposed moving its next run to a printer outside the city. Mr. Ashcombe worries that an advance edition would follow the Chronicle wherever it is read. He will decide after the pressroom inspection this evening.

At noon the early issue’s report of smoke changed. It now says the crowd was assembled for news of a fire that had not occurred. The title of the closure notice did not change. Dr. Saye says the final line of that notice remains too faint to read.
